data.narrative:
Orbit Fab is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Daniel Faber and Jeremy Schiel that has raised $28.5M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comparison universe of 5 public Space & Aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-market comparables including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Given data constraints, only stage-progression methodology proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($28.5M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement yielded an implied valuation of $57M. Public-comp anchoring was inapplicable due to lack of disclosed revenue; the Space & Aerospace sector median P/S of 27.4x across 6 public tickers cannot be used without the target's revenue figure. Peer-median triangulation was similarly inapplicable, as the narrow filtered peer set contained fewer than 3 datapoints despite 14 same-sector companies existing in the broader universe.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $48M to $66M, with a midpoint of $57M. This single-method derivation carries material uncertainty around two key unknowns: Orbit Fab's current revenue (or revenue trajectory), which would unlock public-comp validation, and availability of closer-stage private comparables with disclosed valuations. Conviction in this range is accordingly limited; additional data on revenue and tighter private peer metrics would materially sharpen the estimate.
